name: Belgrade Nikola Tesla Airport
before:
Serbia's main airport, 18 km west of downtown Belgrade near Surčin, run by Vinci Airports. It is the hub for Air Serbia and one of Wizz Air's many operating bases.

There are two terminals joined by a hallway, with 90 check in counters and 32 gates between them. Twenty four of those gates have jetways; the rest are bus gates. One gate, A11, is set aside for domestic flights to Niš.

Terminal 1 is the original building and was renovated in 2016 and 2017. It has largely handled low cost and charter international flights. Terminal 2, built in 1979 and rated for 5 million passengers, has been renovated twice, most recently in 2012 and 2013.

The terminal allocation is not settled. It is believed, though not confirmed, that foreign carriers will use the overhauled Terminal 1 while Air Serbia takes Terminal 2, so check before advising a client which building to use.

The airport is named after Nikola Tesla and connects to the A3 motorway.
